articles.headline: Sources: Eagles' Jalen Hurts, out indefinitely with blood clot, not planned for IR
articles.description: The Eagles are not planning to put Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, sources told ESPN, even as he remains sidelined indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：イーグルスのジェイレン・ハーツ、血栓により無期限欠場、IR入りは予定せず
articles.descriptionJa: イーグルスは、ジェイレン・ハーツが表在性血栓により無期限の戦線離脱を余儀なくされているものの、彼をIR（負傷者リスト）に登録する予定はないと関係者がESPNに語った。
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are not planning to place quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, sources told ESPN, even as he remains sidelined indefinitely because of a superficial blood clot.

The team, according to sources, has not even discussed the possibility of injured reserve, which would sideline Hurts for a minimum of four weeks.

Hurts and the Eagles are still gathering more information and seeking additional medical opinions, with the quarterback's health the foremost consideration. They believe the blood clot is treatable, with Hurts trying to determine the best course, sources said. The ultimate decision about when Hurts returns to play will come from his medical team, and the Eagles are ready to follow his lead. There is still a chance Hurts eventually ends up on injured reserve, if that is the direction the medical information leads them.

In most cases, blood clots are treated with anticoagulants, otherwise known as blood thinners. A player cannot play while on blood thinners.

In general, the minimum timeframe for a moderate dose of anticoagulants is six weeks, sources said. There is a possibility, if the clot is minor enough, that doctors begin with anti-inflammatories only while continuing to monitor. If the clot were to move, as the team said happened in Hurts' case, blood thinners are often the answer. If the clot were to worsen, blood thinners for roughly three months would be the next course of action.

While some around the team might consider Hurts week-to-week, other doctors around the NFL -- who have not examined Hurts -- believe the blood clot could sideline him several weeks. One team's doctor texted ESPN: "It is a broad range and nuance based on size and location and hematology evaluation, but could be six weeks." Another team's doctor had a similar estimation.

The Eagles released a lengthy statement Thursday detailing the process that led to the discovery of the blood clot and Hurts being ruled out for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.

While Hurts has been receiving treatment, the Eagles have been working to fortify their roster. Backup quarterback Tanner McKee will start against the Panthers, and rookie QB Cole Payton was promoted to backup. Philadelphia also signed quarterback Joe Milton off Dallas' practice squad. By NFL rules, Milton must be on the Eagles' roster for three weeks.

This is just the latest sequence in what has been a chaotic stretch for the organization that has included hamstring injuries to running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith, the retirement of future Hall of Fame offensive tackle Lane Johnson, and the trade of Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens.

The Eagles believe Barkley returning next week is realistic, but he has been ruled out for Sunday's game.

articles.headline: José Mourinho praises Vinícius Júnior's Real Madrid grit: If I were him, I'd have left
articles.description: José Mourinho has claimed that if he were Vinícius Júnior, he'd have left Real Madrid last summer, praising the forward's mentality in trying to turn his situation at the club around.
articles.headlineJa: ジョゼ・モウリーニョ、ヴィニシウス・ジュニオールのレアル・マドリードでの粘りに称賛：「もし私が彼なら、去っていただろう」
articles.descriptionJa: ジョゼ・モウリーニョは、もし自分がヴィニシウス・ジュニオールだったら昨夏にレアル・マドリードを去っていただろうと語り、クラブでの状況を好転させようとするフォワードの精神力を称賛した。
articles.body:
José Mourinho has claimed that if he were Vinícius Júnior, he'd have left Real Madrid last summer, praising the forward's mentality in trying to turn his situation at the club around.

Vinícius is currently serving a four-game ban in LaLiga after he reacted angrily to being red carded against Villarreal last Saturday, and then admitted to being unhappy at being substituted early in Madrid's 4-3 comeback win at Roma in midweek.

The Brazil international -- who was key to Madrid's Champions League-winning teams in 2022 and 2024, making himself a Ballon d'Or contender -- has endured a dip in form in recent seasons, being whistled by fans at the Bernabéu, but committed his long-term future to the club in August when he signed a new contract until 2032.

"If I were [Vinícius], in his place, I probably wouldn't be here," Mourinho said in a news conference on Saturday ahead of Madrid's LaLiga game with Sevilla.

"Last summer I would have forced my exit to a league, to a country, to clubs and stadiums where they'd respect him. But because he's a Madrid fan, he has love for the club and the city, he believes things can always improve, he renewed, and he'll keep that smile. I think there's nothing or no-one that can take that away, that joy for living and working. He's a great boy."

Asked to clarify his comments, Mourinho added: "When he signed that contract, he signed it because Madrid is his home, and Real Madrid is his home.

"He's one of the main sources of joy in that dressing room. What I said before was that I doubt I'd be able -- as a player with lots of options -- I doubt whether I'd be able to have his psychological strength, to hold on."

Mourinho substituted Vinícius after 59 minutes at Roma on Wednesday, with Madrid 3-1 down, and Vinicius having given the ball away for Roma's second goal. Youngster Endrick replaced him and inspired a dramatic comeback win -- scoring one goal and providing the assist for another -- and was later named the player of the match.

"Vinícius had a very difficult game," Mourinho admitted. "The guilty party above all was [Roma coach] Gasperini. They attacked us on one wing. They attacked only down their right, with [Matias] Soulé, Wesley, [Gianluca] Mancini, against [Marc] Cucurella and Vinícius.

We knew about their man-to-man pressing, and there, Vini had to keep the ball, or win a foul, but never do what he did. But that's it. It's OK.

Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Broncos beat the Seahawks in overtime Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks three underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out three wild-card predictions.

Could the Texans pull off an upset in London? How many sacks will Chiefs defensive tackle Chris Jones have against the Chargers? Could Rams tight end Tyler Higbee be a sneaky play in fantasy? Will Falcons wide receiver Drake London find the end zone for the first time this season? And will Aaron Rodgers move up in the NFL record books against the Bucs? Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

Fantasy sleepers, surprises

Maldonado predicts three upsets

Dallas Cowboys +1.5 (+102) at Green Bay Packers

The Packers have allowed the eighth-fewest passing yards per attempt this season, but this matchup presents a much tougher test than the backup quarterbacks they've faced in the past two weeks. The Cowboys convert nearly half their third downs and lead the league in the percentage of possessions producing points. Green Bay can hit big plays, but the Cowboys have enough on offense with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to answer.

New York Giants +1.5 (108 moneyline) vs. New Orleans Saints

The Giants have a way to make this Sunday easier for quarterback Jameis Winston. They can run against a struggling Saints defense, then move tight end Isaiah Likely out wide for easy throws over smaller defenders.

On the other side, Saints QB Tyler Shough has struggled even when he has time to throw. So New York doesn't need to constantly pressure him to get stops. That gives the Giants enough to keep this close and win at home.

Houston Texans +3 (+120 moneyline) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Jacksonville's defense is allowing just 14 points per game, but opponents are still finding room to throw. The Jaguars allow 7.7 yards per attempt and 93.2 yards per game to No. 1 receivers, giving QB C.J. Stroud and WR Nico Collins a matchup to attack in London on Sunday.

Houston can also pressure Trevor Lawrence without blitzing or disguising its coverage, making it harder for the quarterback to read the defense. That gives the Texans a way to get stops while leaving more players in coverage.

articles.headline: Rams can't seem to fix their special teams
articles.description: Special teams have played a significant role in five of the Rams' nine losses since the start of last season, including the playoffs.
articles.headlineJa: ラムス、スペシャルチームの立て直しが進まず
articles.descriptionJa: 前シーズンの開幕からプレーオフを含め、ラムスの9敗のうち5回においてスペシャルチームが大きな要因となっている。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The Rams entered this season as Super Bowl favorites, but their special teams unit has been a big part of what has kept Los Angeles' "superteam" from having success.

As Rams head coach Sean McVay tries to fix the issues for the unit in-season, he said he has leaned on a lesson from former Rams defensive coordinator Wade Phillips.

"If it's important enough to you, you'll get it done."

The Rams enter Week 6 with a minus-15.3% special teams DVOA, which would be the worst in history over a full season.

One of the first attempts to fix the unit came Oct. 2 when the Rams cut returner Xavier Smith. The second came Tuesday, when the Rams released kicker Harrison Mevis.

The previous day, Mevis missed a 50-yard field goal attempt in the first quarter of the Rams' loss to the Buffalo Bills and had a potential winning field goal blocked in overtime. The kicks were the fourth and fifth failed kicks by Mevis this season, giving him a 56% field goal rate (5-of-9). That is the lowest field goal percentage in the NFL.

The Rams replaced Mevis with Blake Grupe, whom they signed off of the New York Jets' practice squad.

"Ultimately, we need better production, and that's what we're hoping to get [from] Blake," McVay said.

Grupe split his 2025 season with the New Orleans Saints and the Indianapolis Colts. Grupe, who spent the first 45 games of his career with the Saints, was cut after going 18-of-26 on field goals with New Orleans in 2025.

He spent the final five games with the Colts, where he made all 11 of his field goal attempts and all 10 extra points.

Grupe called that time in Indianapolis "a big stint in my career," saying he was able to show what he could do.

"I hit the ground running," Grupe said. "We had a rainy game in Jacksonville, so it definitely wasn't an easy first one, but we got out there, we got to work, got the ball rolling.

"Those five weeks in Indy were seriously big for me, big for my career."

The kicking woes are not an issue isolated to this season. The Rams have a 77.2 field goal percentage over the past four seasons, the second worst in NFL over that span, according to ESPN Research.

"There's a lot that goes into special teams," Grupe said. "Guys got to cover. We got to put the ball where it's supposed to be. You've got to have elite specialists play to be elite on special teams. So I feel like I can do that.

"There's a lot of things that we can do on kickoff and bring some consistency in the field goal game."

Special teams have played a significant role in five of the Rams' nine losses since the start of last season, including the playoffs. After the Rams allowed a 58-yard punt return touchdown that sparked a 16-point comeback by the Seattle Seahawks in Week 16, McVay fired special teams coordinator Chase Blackburn.

articles.headline: Ravens believe Browns' Todd Monken wants 'to kick our tail'
articles.description: When Cleveland's coach takes the sideline Sunday, Baltimore players will face off against their fiery former OC.
articles.headlineJa: レイブンズ、ブラウンズのトッド・モンケンは「我々を叩きのめしたい」と考えていると確信
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日にクリーブランドのコーチがサイドラインに立つ際、ボルティモアの選手たちは、かつて自分たちを率いた情熱的な元OCと対峙することになる。
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Many in the Baltimore Ravens' locker room believe Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken is not being entirely truthful about Sunday's reunion.

Monken, who was Baltimore's offensive coordinator the previous three seasons, insisted this week that there are no added emotions in facing his former team. But the Ravens feel they know exactly what this game means to the usually fiery Monken.

"If I know Todd the way I think I know Todd, he will want to kick our tail," Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey said.

Despite great success in 2023 and 2024, Monken exited Baltimore nine months ago amid conflicting reports about his relationship with players, especially with quarterback Lamar Jackson, who isn't expected to play Sunday because of an ankle injury. During the 2025 season, when the offense dropped to the middle of the NFL, there were anonymous sources who voiced the players' discontent with Monken's playcalling.

In the offseason, Monken stressed there were no issues between him and Jackson. After Monken was hired by the Browns in January, he received congratulatory texts from Ravens players, including Jackson.

Now, after leading the Browns (3-2) to their best start in five years, Monken is facing the Ravens (4-1) in an early-season battle for first place in the AFC North (1 p.m. ET, CBS).

"He might not say it in the media, but to the team he definitely talks a lot of trash and lets them know [that] he wants to beat us," Ravens running back Derrick Henry said.

During his time in Baltimore, Monken elevated the Ravens' offense to new heights. In 2023, he helped Jackson to his second NFL Most Valuable Player award. The next season, Monken led the Ravens' offense to its first No. 1 ranking in the NFL.

But in 2025, the Ravens unraveled in a disappointing 8-9 season. With Jackson struggling with injuries, Baltimore finished with 311.8 yards per game, which was its fewest in eight years.

Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman said he felt Monken left on good terms, pointing out the impressive production and records set under him.

"When you are a player, you have to make the choice whether you want to make this game about Todd Monken or do you want to make it about going to play football," Bateman said. "I am pretty sure Todd Monken is not worried about Rashod Bateman or what he has done in Baltimore. He is worried about getting the Cleveland Browns right to beat us. So, I think for both sides, the respect is mutual."

Monken feels grateful for how the Ravens handled his final month with the team, and the Ravens can be thankful to Monken for how he helped them land his successor with an influential phone call to Declan Doyle.  

In January, Monken was allowed to work at the Ravens' facility after John Harbaugh was fired as head coach. He had his initial virtual meeting with the Browns while sitting in his Ravens office.

articles.headline: Why is Chargers RB Omarion Hampton's snap count decreasing?
articles.description: Coach Jim Harbaugh and OC Mike McDaniel on why RB Omarion Hampton is being used differently.
articles.headlineJa: チャージャーズのRBオマリオン・ハンプトン、なぜスナップ数が減少しているのか？
articles.descriptionJa: RBオマリオン・ハンプトンの起用法が変化している理由について、ジム・ハーボーHCとマイク・マクダニエルOCが語る。
articles.body:
For all intents and purposes, when the Los Angeles Chargers selected running back Omarion Hampton with the No. 22 pick in the 2025 NFL draft, it seemed a perfect fit.

Hampton provided the physical, bruising style of running so often associated with coach Jim Harbaugh's teams. He was the type of three- or even four-down back that the front office envisioned pairing with quarterback Justin Herbert.

But less than two seasons in, it's been more flashes than a surefire bet.

A fractured left ankle early in the season and a right ankle injury late hampered his rookie campaign, but Hampton produced when on the field with 545 yards and a team-high four touchdowns. With offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel hired in January, Hampton's role seemingly neared a breakout in a new wide-zone-heavy run scheme.

The former Miami Dolphins coach compared Hampton to Hall of Fame running back Terrell Davis. And after a week of training camp, McDaniel highlighted Hampton as a player with as much growth as, if not more than, any player.

The proof hasn't been in the pudding so far.

This season, Hampton's snap count has decreased since having 40 in Week 2 against the Las Vegas Raiders. Hampton also had a career-high 23 carries in that game. Since then, his numbers have dropped, going to 20 snaps against the Denver Broncos in Week 5 -- the fewest offensive snaps among the running back room of Kimani Vidal (26) and Keaton Mitchell (21).

However, that isn't hindering Harbaugh's confidence in Hampton. Harbaugh said that Hampton is "playing extremely well in all phases." But, if that is true, then why the decrease in usage?

"Yeah, hard to predict how many [snaps] a player is going to get but yeah, every time Omarion is in the game, I'm fired up," Harbaugh said Wednesday. "Kimani played really really good football too. And Keaton as well. There's three outstanding backs, but love them, love them all."

Following a Week 4 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, Harbaugh didn't explain why the running back share changed in Week 3.

Hampton had a costly fumble against the Raiders, his second of the season. Then in Week 3, he dropped to 27 snaps against the Buffalo Bills. Then, he played 22 snaps versus Seattle. Harbaugh said the rotation is what they thought was best for the team and wanted to utilize the skills of three running backs who are "all playing good."

From a statistical standpoint, Hampton's numbers aren't far off through five games this season compared to last. He currently has a team-high 73 carries for 271 yards as opposed to 66 carries for 314 yards last year. His runs have been deemed a "rush success" 37% of the time so far, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. That figure was at 42% in 2025.

articles.headline: Is Martínez's outburst a sign of chaos to come for Man United and Carrick?
articles.description: Michael Carrick insists his team is ready to move past Lisandro Martínez's fiery midweek comments. Only a win Sunday vs. Leeds will prove him right.
articles.headlineJa: マルティネスの爆発は、マン・Uとキャリックにとって混乱の前兆か？
articles.descriptionJa: マイケル・キャリックは、チームはリサンドロ・マルティネスが週半ばに行った激しい発言を乗り越える準備ができていると主張している。日曜日のリーズ戦での勝利のみが、彼の正しさを証明することになる。
articles.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- Michael Carrick walked into the media room at Manchester United's Carrington training ground Friday like a man on a mission.

Knowing that he would face questions about defender Lisandro Martínez's explosive interview in the wake of the 2-0 UEFA Champions League defeat to Atlético Madrid, the head coach came prepared with a rebuttal.

After Martínez took aim at director of football Jason Wilcox, the strength of the squad and, by extension, some of his teammates Tuesday, Carrick set about painting a picture of unity.

"We've moved on," he said. "This morning there was a really good feeling around the squad. ... I have to say, they were in really good spirits and trained really well, so we've moved on pretty quickly.

"Sometimes someone says something that's a little bit, maybe shouldn't say it at a certain time, but that doesn't distract us from what we're creating here and the environment and the spirit within the group. It's not affected."

Carrick dismissed a suggestion from former teammate Wayne Rooney that Martínez's comments could "rip the dressing room apart" and tried to flip the script by saying the controversy could "galvanize" the group. Only time will tell if that's the case -- starting with the trip to Leeds United on Sunday.

Martínez is available to play at Elland Road after talks with Carrick, Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada on Thursday resulted in an apology, a fine and nothing more. The club has been keen to move on as quickly as possible, but the episode will only fuel a feeling of restlessness behind the scenes amid a difficult start to the campaign.

United bosses, according to ESPN sources, are more concerned that Martínez chose to air his criticism so publicly rather than the actual content of the interview. There's an acceptance internally that the squad has its weaknesses, particularly at left back. In that sense, there is broad agreement when Martínez said the current group is not "ready for this kind of night" -- a reference to the challenge of facing an Atlético Madrid team that reached the semifinals of the Champions League last season.

A key frustration for the club's executive branch is that it believes it has created an atmosphere in which these conversations can be had face-to-face. The £50 million revamp of Carrington, completed in August 2025, has seen Wilcox and Berrada spend more time at the training ground.

In the past, United's executives would work from offices in the east stand at Old Trafford, keeping their distance from the players and football staff. The idea behind the new, more integrated Carrington was that it would allow for better communication between departments. One source said that Martínez deciding to go public was a "bizarre approach."

Trending rumors

- Wantaway Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel's next destination will be revealed soon, reports Spanish newspaper Diario Sport, with Real Madrid and Barcelona the clear frontrunners over Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich. The 16-year-old is still training alone in a town just outside Barcelona as he looks for a move away from United. His agent, Ali Barat, has compiled the offers from clubs interested in Gabriel. Madrid are willing to accept the terms presented by the player and agent, which would see the deal come to €10 million and include a three-year contract plus various bonuses, although there are more uncertainties when it comes to Barça.

The Bees would demand over £60 million if the 24-year-old was to leave in January, and while the aforementioned pair have the most interest, Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and United have been linked with him. Brentford feel no pressure to let Schade leave and have even opened talks about a new contract, with his current deal expiring in 2028.

- Bayern Munich's longstanding interest in Barcelona attacking midfielder Dani Olmo remains, reports Diario Sport. That interest has been added to by the possibility that Michael Olise and Jamal Musiala could leave the Bundesliga giants in the summer. Even so, Bayern haven't made a formal offer for the 28-year-old, and there isn't one expected in the short term. A departure from Barcelona also seems unlikely for the Spain international at this point, as it would take a substantial offer for Barça to even consider letting him leave.

- Manchester United are closely monitoring Bazoumana Touré despite the winger only joining Newcastle United from Hoffenheim for around £43 million in the summer, according to TEAMtalk. Arsenal are also keeping a close eye on the 20-year-old's progress with both sides having tracked Touré before he joined the Magpies. There is interest from back in Germany, while Tottenham and Aston Villa are also monitoring the Ivory Coast international, although none of the clubs have made a formal approach or will do until at least the summer.

articles.headlineJa: ジェームズとエムビードがセブンティシクサーズのプレシーズン最終戦に出場、「まだリズムを整えている最中」
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜夜のセルティックス戦（125-120で敗戦）を欠場したVJエッジコム不在の中、レブロン・ジェームズとジョエル・エムビードがプレシーズン最多の出場時間を記録するなど、ニック・ナース監督率いるセブンティシクサーズは今シーズンのチームの姿を垣間見せる展開となった。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- As the Philadelphia 76ers begin a season with a star-laden roster, center Joel Embiid rejects the narrative that anyone needs to sacrifice for this team to succeed.

"I'm against the concept of sacrificing," he said after Friday's preseason finale. "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat."

Albeit without second-year starting guard VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday's 125-120 loss to the Boston Celtics for precautionary reasons, Sixers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what this Sixers team may look like this season.

The other active Sixers starters -- LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Embiid -- all played preseason highs in minutes and well into the second half. Embiid, who struggled in his last appearance two games ago against the Brooklyn Nets, finishing with six points and eight turnovers, was dominant.​

He scored 27 points, grabbed eight rebounds and added five assists. In the third quarter, he had one of the game's best highlights when he threw down an emphatic dunk that drew roars from fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena. "It's good to dunk. I thought I would never dunk again," Embiid said with a smile. "I guess I don't know what happened. I kind of got possessed."

Still, the group never looked comfortable together on the floor, despite playing against Celtics reserves. After the game, players didn't shy away from their somewhat disjointed performance. Brown pointed to the team's spacing Friday night, which he said led to turnovers, as one of the many things they need to fix moving forward.

"We're not where we want to be yet," he said. "So that's just a part of it. It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day."

James echoed Brown's comments, but neither seemed concerned about the Sixers' ability to eventually jell.

"We're getting there," James said. "I mean, obviously we are a couple of weeks in, so we're still working on our rhythm, working on our kinks, and it's not going to be perfect."

The Sixers open the regular season against the New York Knicks on Tuesday.

articles.body:
Liverpool are in pole position to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, while Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae is on the radar of Arsenal. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool are in pole position to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, according to the Daily Mail. The 23-year-old, whose transfer is valued at £100 million, has drawn widespread interest from major clubs including Chelsea, though he is currently sidelined after sustaining an injury on his full England debut. But Liverpool are confident that having former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola in charge will help their case.

- Arsenal are interested in signing Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae during the January transfer window, reports Bild's Christian Falk. The Gunners are seeking defensive cover following an injury to Piero Hincapié, though the 29-year-old South Korea international could also be offered a contract extension to remain in Bavaria.

- Should a January deal for Scott fall through, Liverpool have compiled scouting dossiers on AS Monaco's Lamine Camara and Roma's Manu Koné, TEAMtalk reports. However, the Reds face competition for €55 million-rated Camara -- with Chelsea maintaining interest alongside Aston Villa, Newcastle United, Crystal Palace and Brighton & Hove Albion -- while Koné has been linked with Real Madrid, Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United.

- USMNT prospect Mathis Albert is considering leaving Borussia Dortmund to secure regular first-team minutes, according to Sky Sports Deutschland. The 17-year-old winger has only made one appearance in the German Cup this season. He previously attracted interest from Paris Saint-Germain in 2025, while Manchester City and Chelsea were also looking at signing him for around €20 million.

- Tottenham Hotspur will demand a £75 million fee to consider letting right back Pedro Porro move to Barcelona or Real Madrid, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old signed a five-year contract extension in the summer, significantly strengthening Spurs' position as they aim to retain him past 2027.

Other rumors

- Ex-Liverpool star Steven Gerrard could take over at Wrexham, as current boss Phil Parkinson is under increasing pressure at the Championship club. (TalkSPORT)

- Former Manchester United winger Jadon Sancho, who is now a free agent, is weighing up a formal contract proposal from LaLiga side Getafe. (Times)

- Real Madrid midfielder Arda Guler, 21, has agreed a new deal amid interest from Arsenal and Manchester City. (TEAMtalk)

articles.headline: Xabi Alonso not ready to say if Chelsea heading 'right way'
articles.description: Xabi Alonso said it is too early to tell whether Chelsea are going the "right way" as he looks for greater balance from his free-scoring team.
articles.headlineJa: シャビ・アロンソ、チェルシーが「正しい方向」に向かっているかは判断せず
articles.descriptionJa: シャビ・アロンソは、得点力の高い自身のチームにさらなるバランスを求めており、チェルシーが「正しい方向」に向かっているかを判断するにはまだ早すぎると述べた。
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso said it is too early to tell whether Chelsea are going the "right way" as he looks for greater balance from his free-scoring team.

A chaotic start to life under the Spanish coach sees the Blues sit as the third-highest scorers in the Premier League with 15 goals from their six games, yet no team in the division has conceded more than their 13.

- Alonso: Reece James may be out beyond Christmas

- Ranked: Who are the best 50 players in the Premier League so far this season?

- Moisés Caicedo determined to repay Alonso's faith

In total there have been 28 goals scored in Chelsea's league games so far with six more coming in last weekend's 5-1 win over Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

"You need a lot of clean sheets to win trophies," Alonso said. "But you need to score a lot of goals. So it's about being strong in defence, being good in attack and we are in that process.

"We are still early days. This first part we've been doing good things, other things to be improved. To do a very deep analysis, it's too early probably.

"In February we will have enough game to see where we are going and if it's the right way. But we are demanding in terms of what we are doing and what we can do better."

Much of the issue in conceding goals has come from a lack of control in midfield, a problem that appeared largely to have been fixed on Saturday as Moisés Caicedo made his first start of the season.

The return of the Ecuador midfielder after a calf injury brought far greater stability in the middle of the pitch, with Jordan Henderson, who scored his first two goals for the club as the Cherries were routed, also influential alongside him.

The pair are likely to be used together more than had been planned in the coming weeks with Reece James likely to be out until the new year after undergoing what the club called "minor" surgery on a knee problem.

"It's one game, but we saw positives," Alonso said. "Moises helps Hendo, Hendo helps Moises. I think as well Rom [Roméo] Lavia is in a good moment. He played 25 minutes and he did really well. We need not just two midfielders, we need more than that.

"In terms of personalities, they match well. Hendo he has this energy, he is very active, he covers a lot of pitch. He finds a balance with Moisés who is more in position, he has this stability to be in good distances with everything.

"It was a good start and we need to keep building from that."

Chelsea travel to face Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday knowing that a win will take them above David Moyes' side, with both teams currently on 10 points from six matches.
